bodyPrompt: Edit this windmill picture for a pastoral isometric railway game. Remove the four sails and both crossed stocks completely, with the iron plate where they cross and every shadow they cast. Where they covered the tower and the cap, paint the tower and the cap: continue the cream-stone courses, the window, the slate cap and its eaves exactly as they are around them. On the front of the cap, where the stocks crossed, leave the hub: the short round iron end of the windshaft, standing a little out of the cap toward the lower left, with a dark iron collar. Change nothing else: the tower, the cap, the finial, the window and the door stay exactly as they are, the same size and in the same place. Keep the camera: orthographic 2:1 isometric, no perspective. Light from the upper left. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha 0) and an opaque mill. Never: sails, blades, ground, grass, a plinth, a shadow outside the mill, people, sacks or anything standing apart, text, a border, a glow. References: the second picture is the game's style board: keep to its style.
sailsPrompt: Paint the four sails of this windmill as one picture of their own, over the grey guide, seen face on, looking straight along the windshaft. Two crossed timber stocks make an X along the guide's grey bars, and the square iron plate with four bolts covers their crossing at the exact centre of the picture. On each arm a timber lattice sail as on the reference windmill: the same warm brown timber, the same long frame of rails and bars, beginning about a quarter of the way out from the centre and running to the tip, on the same side of its stock as there. All four sails are alike: each is the next one turned by a quarter turn about the centre, never mirrored. The tips end where the guide's bars end, with a clear margin to the picture's edge. Soft light from the upper left with little contrast: each timber a little lighter on its upper left face and a little darker on its lower and right rims, no shadow cast on another sail, no strong highlight, because the game turns this picture about its centre. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha 0), opaque timber and iron. Never: the tower, the cap, the windshaft, ground, sky, a shadow, motion blur, text, a border, a glow. References: the second picture is the windmill whose sails these are: take their timber, lattice and plate, not their angle. The third is the same mill without its sails: the plate sits on its hub. The fourth is the game's style board.
